title: objectql: a plain `lookup` write accepts a target the writer cannot read — the reference check probes it elevated, and only `master_detail` asks the caller's read door
body:
director#1 · zhuangjianguo · session_01QsR2jV5sBSzCYNEDgpYLJw
Ruled: 6663849489 · letter A (re-affirmed) + delegate read · 2026-11-05T16:47Z (supersedes 6573561091)

## What happens

A write that names a record in a `lookup` field is checked for **existence**, never for **the writer's access to it**. A caller who reads a record as 404 can still store a reference to it.

Measured on `@objectstack/objectql` 18.2.0, live (`objectstack-ai/duly` main 98c188a, `pnpm demo`). The caller is a member whose permission set grants `readScope: 'own'` on the target object `duly_duty` (`sharingModel: 'private'`):

| request (as the member) | answer |
|:--|:--|
| `GET /api/v1/data/duly_duty/<id>` | 404 `RECORD_NOT_FOUND` |
| `POST /api/v1/data/duly_task` with `{ duty: <id> }` (`duty` is `Field.lookup('duly_duty')`) | **201** |
| `PATCH /api/v1/data/duly_task/<own task>` with `{ duty: <id> }` | **200** |
| MCP `create_record` / `update_record` with the same payload | **200** |
| the same POST with an id that exists nowhere | 400 `reference_not_found` |

## Where

`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` (`objectstack` main cae71fed: `assertReferencesResolve` → `referenceExists`, around line 10521). For a plain `lookup` the probe runs under `referenceCheckContext` (`{ ...context, isSystem: true }`, tenant kept). The docblock states the choice: existence "is a fact about the database, not about the caller's row-level visibility", and refusing an unreadable target "would make the platform's own admin flows fail".

#22519 (ruling A) made the exception for `master_detail`. `masterDetailHeaderExists` asks the caller's read door first, and an unreadable header answers `reference_not_found`. The docblock then says "⛔ A plain `lookup` keeps the elevated probe above, unchanged" and "the plain `lookup` probe is not this rule's". The one-hop read for validation predicates (`resolveOneHopRelated`, `authority: 'predicate'`) is also elevated for a tenant-walled target, so a `validations[]` script rule cannot express this either. `lookupFilters` is picker-only.

## Why it matters

- **Integrity, not disclosure.** The write leaks nothing new. The existence oracle is already closed per tenant (#19808), and the probe answers only exists/not. But the stored reference attaches the writer's row to a record they have no business touching. In the measured app, a task's `duty` is part of a unique dispatch identity `(duty, owner, period_key)`. A member who writes ahead of the scheduler on someone else's duty takes that person's period from them.
- **An app cannot declare the rule.** No field key exists for "the writer must be able to read the target". The app's only recourse is a hand-written `beforeInsert`/`beforeUpdate` hook that re-reads the target with `runAs: 'inherit'` and refuses. That hook must also mimic the engine's `reference_not_found` envelope by hand, in one language, because hook text has no translator.

## Asked

A declarable opt-in on a `lookup` field (for example `referenceAccess: 'caller'`, name illustrative) that runs the #22519 caller-read-door check for that field. The elevated default stays for the admin-flow case the docblock names. An unreadable target then answers exactly `reference_not_found`, localized like the engine's own. System writes (`isSystem`) stay exempt, as for `master_detail`.

## Workaround in place

`objectstack-ai/duly#174`: hook `duly_task_duty_readable` on `duly_task` (`runAs: 'inherit'`, compares against the stored value so a re-save is not re-judged). It is meant to be deleted when the platform can declare this.
